Subject: Dedicated capacity — H100 vs A100 vs L4 (initial perf/price data)

Hey Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving toward a dedicated capacity model for our production inference (customer-facing chat + embeddings for search). Before we lock anything down, the execs want a short checklist that ties SKU choices to realistic cost and perf tradeoffs. High level about Celerity:
- Peak qps: ~450 requests/s for chat peaks (short bursts), sustained qps: ~120 req/s
- Average prompt+response: 600 tokens (350 prompt + 250 response)
- Typical p95 latency target: <=220ms for chat; embeddings can be looser
- Context: some long-context analysis (20k tokens) in a small % of requests (~3%)
- Compliance: SOC2 + strict data residency; we’ll need private deployment options and KMS support

We don’t need a full engineering plan yet — a one-page checklist that maps: workload profile -> recommended SKU(s) -> fallback/burst options + quick notes on memory/cost tradeoffs would be ideal. Also include what telemetry you need from our side to finalize a sizing.

Can you send across by EOD next week? Procurement copied.

—Jordan

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear brief. I attached a short SKU fitment checklist (sku-fitment-checklist.pdf) and a capacity workbook you can open (capacity_workbook.xlsx) so we can sketch costed scenarios. Quick notes up front:

- Short answer: for your p95 latency and occasional long context, a blended approach tends to work best — majority A100 reserved for predictable throughput, H100 as a latency-focused failover for very low p95 and large-context batches, and L4 for lower-cost embedding/low-latency burst capacity.

- Memory tradeoffs: H100 gives the highest memory headroom for very long context inference and large multimodal models; A100 is the sweet spot for throughput and overall cost-efficiency; L4 is great for quantized smaller models and embedding-heavy traffic but will increase round-trips for long-context chat.

What we need from Celerity to produce a firm plan:
1) time-series payloads (tokens in/out, avg and p95) for a typical day and for peak days (CSV or the attached workbook format)
2) percent of sessions requiring >8k contexts (or exact context distribution)
3) tolerance for cross-region fallthrough (are you okay with failover to eu-west or us-east if us-west is constrained?)
4) any hard budget constraint (annual committed spend target)

I’ve copied Neha (capacity lead) — she’ll run the preliminary fit and should have a recommendation tomorrow after we get the workbook filled. I also attached the Redwood security questionnaire stub so procurement can start.

Attachments: capacity_workbook.xlsx (stub), sku-fitment-checklist.pdf, security_questionnaire_Celerity.pdf

Rafael / Jonas — I ran quick sizing tests against the workbook assumptions (conservative and optimistic). High-level recommendations below; I attached an annotated checklist (sku-fitment-checklist.pdf) to send to the customer.

1) Baseline (cost-sensitive) — Recommended: Reserved A100 pool (x24 slots) + L4 burst pool (x48)
   - Rationale: A100 x24 handles sustained 120 qps with p95 ~180–210ms for 600-token interactions when using optimized kernels and batching. L4 burst pool covers embeddings and spikes; cheaper per-hour but lower memory so route short-context or embeddings to L4.
   - Memory: A100 (40/80GB depending on sku) gives enough KV cache for 6–8k contexts with quantized models.

2) Performance-first (latency + long context) — Recommended: Reserved A100 pool (x18) + H100 failover (x6) + L4 burst (x24)
   - Rationale: H100 slots used as fast-path for very latency-sensitive long-context jobs and model variants that require large attention memory. With H100 failover enabled, p95 for those paths drops to ~140–170ms. Keep fewer A100s because H100 covers the low-latency tail.

3) Cross-region fallthrough checklist
   - Default: failover reads to nearest redwood region with identical model variant; sticky routing for session affinity for 30 minutes.
   - Constraint: if Celerity requires strict US-only residency, only failover within US regions; otherwise eu-west is an option for capacity hedging.

4) Ops & procurement notes
   - Recommend a 12-month reserved commit for A100 to get predictable unit costs; convert H100 capacity to on-demand or short-term reserved to limit spend.
   - Add autoscale headroom for L4 to 2x for unpredictable embedding spikes.

Attachments referenced: sku-fitment-checklist.pdf, capacity_workbook.xlsx (annotated in our copy). HubSpot note: DL-4892 updated with baseline/perform options.

If Rafael approves, we can send the annotated checklist and a short appendix with costed monthly spend for both scenarios tomorrow.
